summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: The Human Genome Project (1990–2003) sequenced the 3.1647 billion bp human genome (~20,000–25,000 genes). Key findings: <2% codes for proteins, 99.9% nucleotide identity across all humans, largest gene is Dystrophin (2.4 Mb), Chromosome 1 has most genes (2,968), and Y chromosome has fewest (231). DNA Fingerprinting (Alec Jeffreys, 1985) utilizes hypervariable non-coding VNTR minisatellites (11–60 bp) detected via Southern Blotting.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
HGP SALIENT FINDINGS
                          
   Total Human Genome Size  ──► 3.1647 x 10⁹ base pairs (3.16 Billion bp)
   Total Gene Count         ──► ~20,000--25,000 genes (Much lower than expected!)
   Average Gene Size        ──► 3,000 bp (Largest: Dystrophin gene = 2.4 Million bp)
   Protein-Coding DNA       ──► < 2% of the genome
   Chromosome Extremes      ──► Chromosome 1 has MOST genes (2,968); Y Chromosome has FEWEST (231)
   Nucleotide Identity      ──► 99.9% identical in all human beings
   SNPs (Single Nucleotide) ──► 1.4 Million SNP locations identified
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 10.1 Human Genome Project (HGP) Methodologies
1. **Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs)**: Focused on identifying and sequencing all genes expressed as RNA transcripts.
2. **Sequence Annotation**: Sequenced the entire genome (coding and non-coding) followed by functional assignment using automated Sanger sequencers and cloning in **BAC (Bacterial Artificial Chromosomes)** and **YAC (Yeast Artificial Chromosomes)** vectors.
3. **International Rice Genome Sequencing Project (IRGSP)**: Completed in 2004 (*Oryza sativa* - $430\text{ Mb}$ genome, $\approx 37,500\text{ genes}$). Model monocot crop.

### 10.2 DNA Fingerprinting Workflow (Alec Jeffreys, 1985)

```
                      DNA FINGERPRINTING WORKFLOW
                      
   1. Isolation of Genomic DNA (Blood, Hair follicle, Semen)
                           │
   2. Restriction Digestion using Restriction Endonucleases
                           │
   3. Gel Electrophoresis (Separates fragments by size on Agarose Gel)
                           │
   4. Southern Blotting (Transfers DNA fragments to Nylon/Nitrocellulose membrane)
                           │
   5. Hybridization using radiolabeled ³²P-VNTR Probes
                           │
   6. Autoradiography (X-Ray film exposure reveals individual-specific band patterns)
```

- **Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTRs)**: Belong to the **minisatellite** class of non-coding repetitive DNA ($11\text{--}60\text{ bp}$ repeat units). Highly polymorphic among individuals due to unequal crossing over.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Microsatellites (STRs) in Modern Forensics
conceptBreakdown.title: Microsatellites (STRs) in Modern Forensics
conceptBreakdown.content: Modern forensic DNA typing utilizes Short Tandem Repeats (STRs / Microsatellites, 2-6 bp repeats) amplified via multiplex PCR and analyzed by capillary electrophoresis with automated fluorescent detection (CODIS 20 core loci).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Lalji Singh and Indian DNA Fingerprinting
conceptBreakdown.title: Lalji Singh and Indian DNA Fingerprinting
conceptBreakdown.content: Dr. Lalji Singh (Father of Indian DNA Fingerprinting) developed indigenous Bkm (Banded krait minor) satellite DNA probes for forensic and paternity applications in India.
